title: MetricDefinition
description: One canonical metric definition (see ../reporting/REPORTING_SPEC.md and ../reporting/METRICS_CATALOG.md). Every number rendered on any dashboard, report, or alert resolves to exactly one entry of this type. Charts may not compute metrics inline — this file is the single source of truth so two screens cannot disagree about what 'edit-survival' means.

metric_id.description: Stable snake_case identifier. Referenced by dashboards, alerts, and report templates. Never reused for a different meaning — deprecate and mint a new id instead.

name.description: Display name as it appears on screen.

family.description: Which metric family this belongs to.

definition.description: Plain-language definition, precise enough that two engineers implement it identically.

formula.description: The computation, expressed over named source fields. Numerator and denominator both stated explicitly for any rate.

source.description: Which stream(s) the metric is computed from. Cross-stream metrics join on pursuit_id + target.section_id.

fields.description: Specific fields consumed, e.g. agent_call.cost_usd, feedback_event.edit_reason, review_session.active_ms.

filters.description: The row filters the metric DECLARES, e.g. run.mode == 'live' — documentation of intent, checked for enum validity by the registry test, never executed as code. The resolver applies the production-mode exclusion globally (engine/metrics/walker.py production_only) and each resolver hand-codes its own check/kind filter (P26a P0-10 corrected the earlier 'always applied').

grain.description: The level at which one value of this metric exists. Aggregating below its grain is an error.

dimensions.description: Legal slice-by dimensions, e.g. section_type, claim_tier, edit_reason, model_tier, actor_role, engine_version, pursuit_type.

comparability.description: What must be held constant for two values of this metric to be comparable. Violations are segmented or annotated by the reporting layer, never silently averaged (decision O4).

annotate_on_change.description: Trend charts mark the point where a held-constant dimension changed.

reliability.description: How much weight this number can bear. Low-n metrics that are rendered as percentages are how a pilot talks itself into a conclusion it has no evidence for.

min_n.description: Below this denominator, render as a raw count, not a rate. Default 5 for rates.

estimated.description: true = derived from an approximate input (e.g. passive session timing). Must be labeled as estimated wherever displayed.

confidence_caveat.description: Standing caveat shown with the metric, e.g. win-rate changes at pilot volume are not statistically distinguishable from noise.

known_failure_mode.description: The way this metric misleads when read alone, and the companion metric that corrects it.

target.description: The bar, where one exists. Absent for context-only metrics.

basis.description: Where the number came from. 'baseline' targets resolve against the WP-Zero human baseline capture.

set_after_observation.description: true = deliberately unset until observed data exists (decision Q5 cost posture).

alerting.description: Exception alerting only. A metric without a decision attached to it does not get an alert.

route_to.description: Role or channel. Incident-class alerts (anonymization failure) route to a named human, not a digest.

views.description: Which audience views render this metric.

owner.description: Role accountable for this number being right and for the decision it informs. A metric with no owner is deleted at the next review.

introduced_in.description: Release or date the definition took effect. Changing a formula requires a new metric_id or a dated redefinition note.
